discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Zoller and co-workers showed theoretically (1998) that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model with fully tunable parameters. Bloch and Greiner then observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (Nature 2002), the first clean demonstration that a textbook model of strongly correlated matter could be built and probed in the laboratory. Greiner's and Bloch's quantum-gas microscopes later gave single-atom, single-site imaging of Hubbard systems, revealing antiferromagnetic correlations, string order, many-body localisation and entanglement dynamics directly. Together these works founded analog quantum simulation: a new experimental method that answers long-standing condensed-matter questions (magnetism, localisation, high-temperature superconductivity models) with quantitative control no solid can offer. The approach is now used by hundreds of laboratories and underpins the neutral-atom quantum-computing platforms emerging today. This is a mature, transformative achievement of theory and experiment working hand in hand.
